meaning:
μέλος, -ους, τό
[in LXX chiefly for נֵתַח ;]
a member, limb of the body: 1Co.12:14 12:19 12:26 Eph.4:16 (WH, mg.), Jas.3:5; pl. (as always in cl.), τὰ μ. : Mat.5:29-30, Rom.6:13, 19 7:5, 23 12:4, 1Co.12:12 ff, Col.3:5, Jas.3:6 4:1. Metaphorical, πόρνης, 1Co.6:15; of Christians, μ. ἀλλήλων, Rom.12:5, Eph.4:25; Χριστοῦ, 1Co.6:15; σώματος Χριστοῦ, 1Co.12:27, Eph.5:30.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish…
Also, do not present your members to sin as instruments of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as alive from the dead, and your members as…
Don’t you know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? May it never be!
Therefore putting away falsehood, speak truth each one with his neighbor. For we are members of one another.
Put to death therefore your members which are on the earth: sexual immorality, uncleanness, depraved passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry.
So the tongue is also a little member, and boasts great things. See how a small fire can spread to a large forest!
